fieldFixes.summary: Graham Greenleaf's running census of national data-privacy laws, published in Privacy Laws & Business International Report, counted 172 countries with such laws as at 15 March 2025. That is an average of 3.3 new countries a year since Sweden's 1973 law, rising to 5.4 a year since 2020. His April 2025 biennial assessment, the ninth since 2011, concluded for the first time that revising existing laws now mattered more than enacting new ones. A year-by-year list of all 172 followed in June 2025.

issues: 'Adopted 27 January 1977 while the Bundestag sat in Bonn' confuses the Act's date with a parliamentary vote. 27 January 1977 is the date of signature ('Das vorstehende Gesetz wird hiermit ausgefertigt ... Bonn, den 27. Januar 1977', signed by President Scheel). The gazette, BGBl. I Nr. 7, was issued on 1 February 1977. The Bundestag's votes came earlier, in 1976. The BfDI page's 'verabschiedet am 27. Januar 1977' is loose usage, and the BfDI page even heads the entry '28. Januar 1977'.

'It took effect on 1 January 1978, which is also when the post of Federal Data Protection Commissioner was created' is contradicted by the statute. § 47 BDSG 1977 reads: 'Dieses Gesetz tritt am 1. Januar 1978 in Kraft. Abweichend davon treten in Kraft: ... 2. §§ 17, 18, 28 und 38 am 1. Juli 1977'. § 17 is headed 'Bestellung eines Bundesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz'. So the provisions creating the post took effect on 1 July 1977. The BfDI's own milestone of 1 January 1978 simplifies this. The first commissioner, Hans Peter Bull, took office on 14 February 1978.

Hesse: 'had passed the world's first data-protection law on 7 October 1970' is shaky. 7 October 1970 is the Act's official date (GVBl. I S. 625). The BfDI page cited as source 0 gives 30 September 1970 ('Hessen erlässt ...') and entry into force on 13 October 1970. Secondary sources disagree about the day the Landtag voted, so the wording now avoids 'passed on'.
Regulator label: in 1977 the office was the Bundesbeauftragter für den Datenschutz (BfD). The 'und die Informationsfreiheit' (BfDI) name dates from 2006.

Sources 0 and 1 are the same URL with different titles and institutions. The page's <title> is 'BfDI - Datenschutz-Garten - Die Geschichte des Datenschutzes' and its heading is 'Die Geschichte des Datenschutzes'. Source 1 has been aligned to match.
Checked and correct: BGBl. I S. 201; the Bonn coordinates (Bundeshaus); the HBDI quote on Hesse being first in the world.

fieldFixes.note: The first federal data-protection act. It was signed in Bonn on 27 January 1977 by President Walter Scheel and promulgated in the Federal Law Gazette on 1 February 1977 (BGBl. I S. 201). Most of it took effect on 1 January 1978. The sections providing for a Federal Commissioner for Data Protection (§§ 17–18) took effect earlier, on 1 July 1977, and the first commissioner, Hans Peter Bull, took office on 14 February 1978. Hesse's Data Protection Act, dated 7 October 1970 and in force from 13 October 1970, had been the world's first data-protection law.

issues: 'Passed by the Storting on 9 June 1978' is probably a conflation, though the cited article says so word for word. 9 June 1978 is the Act's official date (LOV-1978-06-09-48). Norwegian Acts of that era are dated by royal sanction in the Council of State, which met on Fridays. 9 June 1978 was a Friday, and other Acts share the date, such as the Equality Act, LOV-1978-06-09-45. The Odelsting and Lagting votes normally came earlier. The actual vote dates could not be found (lovdata.no returns HTTP 405 to scripts), so the note now gives the Act's official date without claiming a Storting vote on that day.
